# Fork-maintained patches for rayward-external/litellm
#
# Upstream (BerriAI/litellm) uses ARG-variable FROM in Dockerfiles.
# Our fork pins literal image@sha256 digests so Scorecard/OpenSSF does not flag them.
# Upstream syncs may revert to ARG-only FROM; daily-patch-verify detects and re-pins.
#
# Format: <file> | <grep_pattern_that_proves_patch_is_present> | <human_description>

Dockerfile            | FROM.*sha256:    | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM); this is the Dockerfile litellm-build-push.yml deploys (Scorecard PinnedDependenciesID)
backend/Dockerfile    | FROM.*sha256:    | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM)
gateway/Dockerfile    | FROM.*sha256:    | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM)
migrations/Dockerfile | FROM.*sha256:    | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM)
.github/workflows/codeql.yml        | timeout-minutes: 90                       | CodeQL analyze job timeout raised 30->90 min so python leg completes
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | py/log-injection                          | Exclude CWE-117 query: taint explosion from pervasive logging; same scaling class as py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data
.github/workflows/alert-bridge.yml  | workflow_dispatch                          | Alert bridge for code-scanning triage; re-apply after -X theirs syncs that wipe .github/workflows/
.github/workflows/alert-bridge.yml  | FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24         | Opt in to Node.js 24 runtime before GitHub's 2026-06-16 forced migration (upload-artifact@v4 is a Node 20 action)
.github/workflows/alert-bridge.yml  | list_secrets                               | mode=list_secrets: reads secret-scanning/alerts through the same security-events:write token scope, since the security-sweep's CCR token cannot call that API directly. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once the CCR/Claude GitHub App token gains secret-scanning-alert read scope directly.
cookbook/livekit_agent_sdk/requirements.txt | json-repair>=0.60.1                  | Explicit pin forcing the livekit-agents[xai] transitive json-repair dependency past GHSA-xf7x-x43h-rpqh (unbounded CPU DoS via circular JSON-schema $ref). REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once livekit-agents itself requires json-repair>=0.60.1.
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | cookbook                                   | paths-ignore: cookbook/ and scripts/benchmark_* are example/benchmark code; excluded to prevent FP CodeQL alerts (py/reflective-xss #953, py/regex-injection #952, py/clear-text-storage #979 #980)
litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py   | re\.escape\(allowed_model_pattern\)        | is_model_allowed_by_pattern: re.escape() the wildcard pattern before building the match regex, closing py/regex-injection (#1024). REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream applies the same escape fix.
litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/litellm_content_filter/content_filter.py | resolved category file path escapes categories_dir | _load_categories: realpath/commonpath containment re-check on category_file_path immediately before use, closing py/path-injection (#1025) as defense-in-depth alongside the existing category_name regex validation. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream applies an equivalent containment check.
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | py/stack-trace-exposure                    | Exclude CWE-209 query: tracebacks only reach loggers, ProxyException.to_dict() never serializes a traceback field, CodeQL cannot distinguish log sinks from HTTP response sinks
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization   | Exclude CWE-184 query: security-critical URL validation uses urlparse() tuple comparison; flagged startswith/endswith are non-security normalization (JWT heuristic, trailing-slash strip)
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | py/request-without-cert-validation          | Exclude CWE-295 query: every httpx client resolves verify via get_ssl_verify()/get_ssl_configuration() (litellm/llms/custom_httpx/http_handler.py), defaulting to True and only disabled via explicit operator opt-in (SSL_VERIFY env var / litellm.ssl_verify / explicit param) for enterprise self-signed/internal-CA deployments; CodeQL cannot follow the dynamic default so it flags every call site

litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py | Applied across all keys for this team\.\n    Example - update team TPM Limit | update_team's docstring documents mcp_rpm_limit (wording copied verbatim from new_team's existing line). UpdateTeamRequest gained the mcp_rpm_limit field upstream but update_team's docstring was never updated, so tests/documentation_tests/test_api_docs.py fails: it diffs a function's docstring against its request model's model_fields. Both the endpoint and the model are IDENTICAL to upstream, so this is upstream breakage, not a fork artifact — upstream's own CI misses it. NOTE the grep pattern is deliberately anchored on the following "Example - update team TPM Limit" line: new_team carries the same sentence, so matching the sentence alone would report this patch present even after a sync drops it. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream documents mcp_rpm_limit in update_team's docstring itself.
litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py | _translate_legacy_thinking_for_adaptive_model | Fork-only legacy thinking.enabled -> adaptive translation (infers an output_config.effort from the legacy budget_tokens, so pre-existing budget_tokens-based callers keep working on adaptive-thinking models) plus its _legacy_thinking_budget_to_effort/_coerce_optional_int helpers and the transform_request call site. Every -X theirs sync so far has silently dropped this (restored three times now: commit 343d3008, the 2026-07-12 sync, and the 2026-07-16 sync); it never conflicts textually with upstream's edits to the surrounding transform_request body, so git's 3-way merge just drops it instead of flagging a conflict. Signatures must be re-checked against upstream's current _is_adaptive_thinking_model/_validate_effort_for_model signatures each time (upstream has added a custom_llm_provider parameter to both since this was first written) — do not copy-paste the old diff verbatim. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream ships equivalent legacy-thinking-to-adaptive translation itself.

.github/workflows/codspeed.yml | continue-on-error: true | rayward-external/litellm was never registered with CodSpeed (codspeed.io) — the "Run benchmarks" step's own pytest-codspeed run passes, but the upload step 401s ("Repository not found or the user does not have access to it") on every PR/push run, so continue-on-error keeps a fork-infra gap from blocking the merge gate. First observed 2026-07-16 (PR #123, the first PR whose base commit made this workflow's checks land on a PR at all). REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once an admin registers rayward-external/litellm with CodSpeed (or adds a working CODSPEED_TOKEN) and the upload step succeeds.
tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_budget_reservation.py | _arelease_max_parallel_requests_on_disconnect = AsyncMock\(\) | Upstream #33736 moved the max_parallel_requests slot release into an async proxy_logging_obj._arelease_max_parallel_requests_on_disconnect() call inside async_streaming_data_generator's disconnect cleanup, but only added coverage in the new tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_common_request_processing.py; this pre-existing sibling file's bare MagicMock() stand-ins for proxy_logging_obj were never given that attribute, so awaiting it raised "TypeError: object MagicMock can't be used in 'await' expression" in 4 tests. Both call sites are IDENTICAL to upstream (verified via `git diff upstream/litellm_internal_staging`), so this reproduces on a clean upstream checkout too — upstream's own CI misses it because the new test file doesn't exercise these older streaming-cancel fixtures. ruff-strict-budget.json | "C901": {\n    "limit": 319 | C901 (cyclomatic-complexity) ceiling bumped 316->319 during the 2026-07-19 upstream sync: scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py attributed 1 new violation to the sync diff itself (upstream commits merged in via -X theirs, not fork-authored code), and the fork's own pre-sync base (ed1ef0fe) was independently already 2 over the 316 cap (318 total) with nobody having caught it, since this gate only runs on pull_request and the base commit landed via a route that never exercised it directly. `make lint-budget-update` only ratchets a rule down when the branch's own count improves on it, so it could not reconcile an over-budget rule; the ceiling was bumped by hand to exactly the verified current total (319), giving zero extra headroom for future fork contributions. The repo's own budget-ratchet job (test-linting.yml) is explicitly documented as non-gating and exists precisely to surface a ceiling raise like this one as a review signal. REMOVAL CONDITION: lower back toward 316 (or below) via a dedicated complexity-reduction pass, or accept future syncs nudging it further if upstream's own complexity keeps growing.

litellm/utils.py | def _client_side_bad_request | Pre-flight request validators (validate_chat_completion_user_messages, validate_chat_completion_tool_choice) raise litellm.BadRequestError instead of a bare Exception. These run in completion() BEFORE a deployment is picked, so a bare Exception could not be mapped by exception_type() and fell through to APIConnectionError: callers got HTTP 500 attributed to whichever provider the router was about to try -- a provider that never saw the request -- and _should_retry(500) then retried a permanently-invalid payload. Diagnosed 2026-07-21 from a live report where a client posted content-part dicts with no "type" key and spent a session chasing a Baseten outage that never happened. model/llm_provider are deliberately empty so no false attribution is reintroduced. Covered by tests/test_litellm/test_utils.py::test_validate_chat_completion_user_messages_raises_bad_request and ::test_validation_bad_request_is_not_remapped_to_api_connection_error (that path, NOT tests/litellm_utils_tests/, is the tree the test-unit `misc` job actually runs). REMOVAL CONDITION: fork-permanent for now. Do NOT open an upstream PR to carry this without the repo owner explicitly asking for one; remove only if upstream ships an equivalent fix on its own.
CLAUDE.md | RAYWARD FORK ONLY | Fork-only "PRs go to THIS fork, never upstream" section pinned at the top of upstream's CLAUDE.md. Both this file and AGENTS.md are SHARED with upstream, so a -X theirs sync silently drops the section and the next agent reads a file that says nothing about PR targets — which is exactly how an unauthorized PR got opened against BerriAI/litellm on 2026-07-21 (closed, branch deleted). REMOVAL CONDITION: none; this is a standing org policy, not a temporary divergence.
AGENTS.md | rayward-external/litellm` only | Fork-only PR-target rule appended to upstream's AGENTS.md, pointing at the CLAUDE.md section above. Same shared-with-upstream drop risk. REMOVAL CONDITION: none; standing org policy.

litellm/types/interactions/generated.py | queued = "queued" | Adds the `queued` member to BOTH Interaction status enums (Status1 lowercase, Status3 uppercase). The file is datamodel-codegen output from https://ai.google.dev/static/api/interactions.openapi.json pinned at 2025-12-16; Google has since added a `queued` status, so the generated enums are stale and a real `status: "queued"` response would fail Pydantic validation at runtime. Added by hand rather than regenerating, to avoid pulling unrelated spec drift into a validation-fix PR — a full datamodel-codegen refresh is worth doing separately. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream regenerates this file against a spec that already includes `queued`.
tests/test_litellm/interactions/test_openapi_compliance.py | "queued", | Adds `queued` to test_status_enum_values' expected list. This test fetches Google's LIVE spec and exact-matches the status enum BY DESIGN — its docstring says the breakage "is how we get notified to review the change". It fired correctly; the review outcome is the generated.py fix above. Fails on upstream too (verified: reverting this branch's code changes reproduces it), so this is upstream breakage surfacing through a live external spec, not a fork artifact. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream updates the expected list itself.
litellm/proxy/litellm_pre_call_utils.py | from litellm.router_strategy.tag_based_routing import | Fork-only hard-provider-pin (P1) + attribution-tag-sanitize (P2) hardening uses PINNED_PROVIDER_ROUTE_KEY, ORIGINAL_REQUEST_TAGS_KEY, ORIGINAL_REQUEST_TAGS_SNAPSHOT_TAKEN_KEY and PIN_TAG_PREFIX from litellm/router_strategy/tag_based_routing.py to strip client-supplied route-pin/tag-snapshot signals from request metadata and re-assert only the trusted request.state-derived pin. The 2026-07-22 -X theirs sync dropped only this import line (the surrounding import block textually conflicted with upstream's own edits, so git's 3-way merge silently resolved without flagging a conflict), leaving all 4 names undefined at module import time — broke every proxy test job's conftest import. Same drop-only-the-import class as the anthropic legacy-thinking translation above. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream ships equivalent pinned-provider-route hardening itself.
litellm-rust/crates/core/Cargo.toml | aws-sdk-sts.*default-https-client | aws-sdk-sts's own "rustls" feature name is misleading: it maps to aws-smithy-runtime's legacy "tls-rustls" feature (hyper 0.14 + rustls 0.21.12 + rustls-webpki 0.101.7), not the modern stack. That legacy webpki was vulnerable to RUSTSEC-2026-0098/0099/0104 (name-constraint bypass and a reachable panic in certificate parsing). Switched the feature request to "default-https-client", which resolves to the same modern rustls-aws-lc/webpki-0.103+ stack that aws-config's own "rustls" feature already uses (aws-config's "rustls" = "client-hyper" = "default-https-client"; only aws-sdk-sts's naming was inconsistent). No code in this workspace references the legacy hyper-0.14 connector directly, so the swap is drop-in. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream smithy-rs renames aws-sdk-sts's "rustls" feature to resolve to the modern stack, matching aws-config, itself.
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization   | Exclude CWE-184 query for JS/TS: same FP class as the existing py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization exclude above, but surfaced in upstream's new co-located ui/litellm-dashboard/**/*.test.tsx files (2026-07-23 sync, e.g. TransformRequestPanel.test.tsx) that assert on rendered DOM text via RTL's getByText(/https:\/\/api\.openai\.com\/.../) — not a security decision on an untrusted URL. Not caught by the existing "tests" paths-ignore entry, which only matches the top-level Python tests/ dir.
ui/litellm-dashboard/eslint-suppressions.json | models-and-endpoints/add/page.tsx | Grandfathers 4 new no-restricted-imports (antd) violations in upstream's own new models-and-endpoints/{add/page,layout,llm-credentials/page}.tsx and vertexCredentialsUpload.ts (2026-07-23 sync). Confirmed upstream breakage: both the antd-ban eslint rule and the violating new files come from upstream itself, and `npx eslint` on a clean upstream/litellm_internal_staging worktree fails identically on these 4 files. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream migrates these files off antd itself (or prune via `eslint . --prune-suppressions` once someone does it fork-side).
.github/workflows/test-litellm-ui-unit.yml | runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n    timeout-minutes: 45 | New workflow from the 2026-07-23 sync (upstream's own PR) requests `ubuntu-latest-16-cores`, a GitHub-hosted larger runner that requires explicit per-org provisioning; rayward-external does not have it configured, so the job queued with runner_id 0 for 50+ minutes and would never run. Swapped to the standard `ubuntu-latest` (used by every other workflow in this repo) and dropped the `--poolOptions.forks.maxForks=14` override (sized for the 16-core runner) so vitest auto-sizes to whatever the runner actually has. Also raised timeout-minutes 20->45: on this sync PR nearly every file changed, so vitest's --changed diff mode ends up running close to the full suite, and the standard runner's smaller core count needs more wall-clock time than the 16-core original assumed (confirmed via a cancelled run that was still steadily passing tests, not hung, when the 20-minute timeout hit). REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once rayward-external provisions ubuntu-latest-16-cores runners (or upstream itself relaxes the runner requirement).
